rubric:
# First-impression craft rubric

A reusable 5-point rubric for evaluating the design craft of any product landing page or signed-out state.

## When to use

Apply this rubric when you want to assess whether a page makes a strong first impression through design quality alone, independent of content strategy or conversion goals.

Establish a craft baseline once per comparable page version. Promise, trust, audience, and other evaluations should reference it rather than request the same six scores again. Revisit only affected craft dimensions when captured evidence changes materially; use a new baseline when the page, rendering context, or rubric is not comparable.

## Dimensions

| # | Dimension | Weight | Question | 5 (best) | 1 (worst) |
|---|-----------|--------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | Visual hierarchy | 1x | Can you identify the primary message and action within 3 seconds? | Instant | Buried |
| 2 | Information density | 1x | Is every element earning its space? | Nothing to remove | Noise competes with signal |
| 3 | Readability | 1x | Do typography, contrast, and sentence length support scanning? | Effortless | Labored |
| 4 | Coherence | 2x | Does the page feel like one designed thing? | Unified | Assembled from parts |
| 5 | Durability | 1x | Would this design hold if content changed by 30%? | Resilient | Brittle |
| 6 | Intentionality | 1x | Can you tell why every design decision was made? | Every choice has a reason | Arbitrary or defaulted |

## Scoring guide

Coherence is weighted 2x. Max score: 35.

- **29-35:** Exceptional craft. Study and reference.
- **22-28:** Solid craft with specific areas to sharpen.
- **15-21:** Functional but lacking intentionality.
- **7-14:** Needs structural rethinking.

## How to apply

1. Open the page cold (no prior context, clear cache if possible).
2. Score each dimension independently, 1-5.
3. Write one sentence per dimension noting what earned or cost the score.
4. Sum the total. Use the scoring guide to frame the verdict.
5. End with two lists: patterns worth borrowing, and anti-patterns to avoid.

For subsequent lenses, link the baseline and its evidence. For a changed-dimension review, record the prior score, new score, and observed change for each reassessed dimension. Preserve unaffected scores as inherited context, not new judgments. Keep AI scores distinct from human overrides, and never transfer scores between page versions without comparing the evidence.

---

*This is a living rubric. Adjust dimensions, weights, or scoring anchors as your evaluation practice evolves.*

issueTitle: LangChain LangGraph signed-out page: first-impression craft
issueBody:
### Bet title

LangChain LangGraph signed-out page: first-impression craft

### Primary lens

Craft

### Target page

https://www.langchain.com/langgraph

### Evaluator class

Design quality (craft, coherence, accessibility)

### Evidence type

Rubric-scored (criteria checklist)

### Design relevance

Compare how agent platforms present their promise, build trust, and earn a first impression for cold, signed-out visitors.

### Suggested evaluation approach

Checked review using the first-impression craft rubric.

ai.summaryMarkdown: The page presents a clear hero: a concise headline "Balance agent control with agency", a short supporting paragraph, and two primary CTAs visible above the fold alongside a decorative waveform motif and a row of customer logos; screenshots confirm a dark theme, strong left-aligned content, and large empty or noisy areas further down the page (including repeated placeholder text in the captured content). Patterns worth borrowing: a single clear hero message with proximate CTAs, a restrained palette and consistent visual motif, and an immediate trust band of customer logos. Anti-patterns to avoid: visible placeholder or repeated dump text that breaks trust, large empty vertical gaps that dilute momentum, and using a coding/monospace font for long body copy which can reduce scanning comfort.

craft.summaryMarkdown: Baseline established for first-impression craft. The hero communicates the primary promise and actions quickly and the page uses a coherent dark-blue visual system, but noisy placeholder content and large empty areas later on reduce polish and signal some content-quality issues that should be fixed before reuse or comparison.

scores.name: Visual hierarchy
scores.rationale: The hero headline, short supporting copy, and two CTAs are visually prominent and findable within seconds, supported by a large decorative waveform that frames the right side of the area.

scores.name: Information density
scores.rationale: Above the fold is clean and purposeful with a clear trust band, but the page contains long vertical spacing and repeated placeholder text lower down that creates noise and reduces the sense that every element earns its space.

scores.name: Readability
scores.rationale: Headlines and CTAs read clearly on the high-contrast dark background, but the site includes JetBrains Mono and some small or dense blocks of text that make longer paragraphs and footer content harder to scan comfortably.

scores.name: Coherence
scores.rationale: The site feels like one designed thing at first glance with a consistent dark theme, blue accents, and shared iconography, though the abrupt presence of placeholder dumps and mismatched content sections weakens the unified experience.

scores.name: Durability
scores.rationale: The modular section structure, clear hero, and restrained visual language suggest the design would survive moderate content changes, but brittle areas include long empty regions and hardcoded filler that could break if copy changes substantially.

scores.name: Intentionality
scores.rationale: Most decisions (hero-first messaging, trust logos, feature callouts) read as deliberate, but the choice of a monospace coding font for general copy and visible placeholder text make some decisions look accidental or unfinished.
